body:
Pass 38. Retracting my Epic 8 recommendation - do not adopt the scope split.

Your gate confirmed runtime_pass FALSE / memory_pass TRUE as I predicted, but my explanation was wrong. I blamed per-support k-by-k solves and built a "<33000 nodes" ceiling on that. The summary refutes it: 1.653e9 factorization units over 3417 s is 4.84e5 units/s. At a conservative 1e8 units/s the whole factorization workload is 16.5 s - 0.48% of measured. Never solve-bound.

Your profiling has it right, and it is my own original finding resurfacing: 59% in repeated whole-frame/support validation - the .validate_relation-per-block-read and SHA-256 overhead I flagged in the first review as an efficiency concern and then failed to connect to this.

If the 7.1x carries from 4096 to 52416: 3417/7.1 + 57.8 = 539 s = 9.0 min against a 30-min gate. Dense metrics would pass at full brain scale. Your rerun is the right call; I will verify it rather than project.

Unaffected: the fixture is still statistically degenerate (84% of supports have k > residual df), so re-run at a meaningful fixture before certifying whatever the runtime turns out to be.
